_note: Sample drift alert rules (Template 16.1 observability + 16.2 four-ledger structure; the sample values are from the book's Anchor & Helm case, your own table should hold absolute numbers). Set the alert line before the budget line, and write the action on breach down in advance. Trigger every alert by hand once before launch. An alarm that does not sound is more dangerous than no alarm.

alerts.threshold: 80% of the budget line (budget line = the post-repair level × 1.5)
80% of the pilot's project-approval estimate line

alerts.action: highest level on the first one, kill criteria (Template 14)
rework retrospective (threshold reuses Template 11.1.4, not invented anew)
rules and prompt retrospective (and the trend is not rising)

alerts.metric: days since the last drill at each dependency point
alerts.action: no change allowed until the drill is made up (Template 16.3)

alerts.metric: sudden shift in the input distribution (e.g. the share of newly registered repair shops)
alerts.action: investigate at the data layer (Template 18.2.2's four retrospective questions)

alerts.metric: sudden shift in the override rate for a single category
alerts.action: check back on that category's rule implementation and list version
